name: The Lava Tubes
hours: Open to the foolish; unmapped, unlit. The Outdoor Club runs one guided trip a term to the first chamber only.
sight: On the volcano's eastern shoulder a collapsed skylight drops into a tunnel as round and smooth as the inside of a pipe, big enough to drive a ferry through. Your torch slides over walls of ropey black glaze and drip-stalactites of frozen lava. The air is cool and mineral and absolutely silent, and side passages branch off at every angle like the roots of a tooth.
things: Climb down the skylight on the knotted rope
Walk the main tube to the first chamber, where the roof glitters
Switch off your torch and experience real dark
Chalk your turnings — everyone who has not is a story
Find the pool of still water that shows no reflection of the roof
Hear, from one side passage only, a faint warm draught and a clicking
Find old chalk arrows in someone else's hand, with dates
secret: Outdoor Club trip Day 38 (unnamed leader; Viktor tags along and vanishes down a side passage). The tubes honeycomb the mountain; one branch runs to within a few metres of the Vault's dome — the warm draught and the clicking. This was Chuck's crack: fifty years ago it was open; a rockfall closed it decades back, and the old chalk arrows in a 24-year-old's hand (dated in a Polish scrawl) still point to it. A week of digging with tools could reopen it: a back way into the Vault that needs no Alpha card — Viktor's long project, and Marrow's engineers' from about Day 120. It is dangerous in the plain sense: bad air in the low sections, a real chance of getting lost (lose a day, be reported absent).
access: Forbidden without the Outdoor Club. The skylight on the east shoulder is reached by the old tramway and lies just outside the area closed on Day 29; the deeper branches run under it.
